messages:
Priya: Alice-Customer opened a support ticket — says their /generate endpoint is ~2x slower after we flipped them to the FP8 calibrated artifact yesterday. They see higher tail latency and a few correctness regressions in long chats. Can eng-runtime/eng-ml triage?
Maya: sorry to hear that, cc Jon and Lee. Do we have the customer id + endpoint?
Priya: customer id CU-9982, endpoint redwood-prod-eu-03, model: gptx-13b-quant-fp8-calib:v2. They rolled from gptx-13b-fp16:v12 -> quant:v2 at 09:04 UTC yesterday.
Jon: thanks. initial guess: calibration range could be producing wider scales, causing heavier dequant math on host or forcing different kernel selection. Also need to check KV cache behavior — FP8 artifacts sometimes change memory layout.
Lee: I pulled prod traces. p50 went 68ms -> 130ms, p95 went 210ms -> 480ms around the promo time. Error rates small but increased timeouts on a few long sessions.
Maya: can you drop the minimal repro and telemetry? Priya, can we get a short failing transcript + a perf trace zipped?
Priya: sent a link to the trace (s3://redwood-support/cu-9982/fp8-trace-176504.zip) and a sample user thread. Customer is sensitive to downtime, they asked for an ETA.
Maya: ok running local repro now. Reproduced locally on a dev gpu with our release image. Script: 
```
# repro
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-quant-fp8-calib:v2","input":"<long chat snippet>","max_tokens":1024,"stream":false}'
```
Maya: Profiling snapshot (shortened):
```
kernel_selector: chosen_path=fp8_mixed_op_fallback
op_time: attention_kv_dequant  +2.7ms
op_time: matmul_fp8_to_fp32 +1.9ms
kv_cache_miss_penalty: 0.9ms per token (changed layout)
batching: avg_batch_size dropped from 8 -> 3 (batch window 8ms unchanged)
```
Jon: interesting — kernel_selector picked a fallback vector path for some ops (fp8_mixed_op_fallback) which ends up doing extra fp32 conversions. That matches the op_time delta. Also lower batch sizes will amplify per-request overhead.
Lee: looking at memory accounting we saw more frequent small memcpy calls that correlate with KV cache shard reorgs after quantization. FP8 artifact uses per-channel quant format that is not memory-aligned in the same way as fp16, causing extra memcpy/pack overhead on our GPU path.
Priya: customer is asking if rolling back to fp16 will revert latency immediately.
Maya: yes rollback to gptx-13b-fp16:v12 will avoid the fp8 conversion path. As an immediate mitigation: route this customer's traffic to dedicated capacity with fp16 model pinned (we can do that now).
Jon: medium-term fixes: (1) fast path kernel for fp8 that avoids host-side dequant for common attention shapes, (2) adjust calibration to use symmetric per-tensor where possible or per-channel with quant alignment padding to match our GPU pack requirements, (3) tweak batching heuristics so small batches are aggregated a little longer for this endpoint.
Priya: I'll propose to customer: (A) immediate: route to fp16 dedicated capacity (no config changes to their app) and open a hotfix rollout; (B) timeline: hotfix for kernel selector + calibration tuning in 48-72h, can we commit?
Maya: we can cut a hotfix branch that forces kernel selection for the attention op to gpu_fp8_fastpath where supported; but need QA on several hardware variants. 48h for a gated rollout seems okay.
Lee: also enabling a KV-cache warmup pass on cold starts will reduce cache miss penalty — send a small burst of canonical completions after deploy. This is low-risk and we can push as a config toggle.
Jon: experiments I ran: switching calibration from 'auto' -> 'per_tensor_symmetric' reduced additional per-token overhead by ~0.9ms and improved sample accuracy for the customer's prompt set. I'll attach my calibration diff.
Maya: notes for SRE: short-term runbook
  - Route CU-9982 to redwood-dedicated-eu-1 (force model=gptx-13b-fp16:v12)
  - Toggle kv_warmup=true for that endpoint
  - Monitor p50/p95 and error rate for next 2h
  - Escalate to eng-ml if regressions persist
Priya: I've asked legal/comms for customer message. Draft to send: "We're sorry for the disruption — we've identified the cause as an interaction between the FP8 calibration artifact and our runtime kernel selection which increased dequant overhead and cache behavior. We will route you to a stable FP16 endpoint immediately and roll out a hotfix in 48-72 hours. Will update in 2 hours with progress." Thoughts?
Jon: good. add that we will run a custom calibration on their eval set to reduce range blow-up and share perf validation.
Maya: QA checklist for hotfix: 
  - unit perf tests across 4 GPU types
  - regression test: sample generation quality on customer's eval set (we have their eval set)
  - perf gate: p95 within 1.2x of baseline fp16 on dedicated hw
Lee: I'll handle the routing and the kv_warmup toggle now. Reporting back in 20m.
deploy-bot: route change applied for CU-9982 -> redwood-dedicated-eu-1 (txn id tx-38721).
Lee: initial metrics look promising: p50 back to ~74ms, p95 dropping from 480 -> 225 after routing. No new errors.
Priya: customer replied: "Thanks. We'll accept the temporary routing and appreciate the update — please keep us posted on the fix timeline." :white_check_mark:
Maya: I'll start the hotfix branch and ping Jon for calibration diffs. Jon, can you post the calibration recipe and the quick perf script you used?
Jon: posting now: 
```
# calibration diff (summary)
- strategy: auto -> per_tensor_symmetric
- clip_percentile: 99.9 -> 99.5
- add alignment_pad=64 for per-channel tables
```

```
# perf check
python perf_check.py --model gptx-13b-quant-fp8-calib:v2 --prompt sample_long_chat.json --runs 50 --collect-kernel-times
```
Jon: saving logs to s3://redwood-support/cu-9982/calib-diffs.log
Maya: thanks. We'll keep this thread for ops + customer updates. If anyone sees other endpoints behaving similarly, please tag this thread.
Priya: noted, I'll close the loop with the customer after the hotfix rollout.
Alice-Customer: thanks team — appreciate the quick action.
